text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired for service=inference-gateway-prod-west1 - metric=http_5xx_rate - threshold=5% - current=12.4% - paging on-call group 'inference-oncall'

pagerduty: Triggered incident INC-8432, responders: @lee, @anya - please ack

lee: acked - taking this. seeing lots of 502/504 from upstream inference pool. starting triage.

anya: ack - on standby for routing checks and can run quick traffic-shift if needed.

lee: quick KV-cache note: some errors show 'kv_timeout' in logs but majority are 502 from model-pool.

mike: FYI saw a deployment in prod-west1 ~30m ago (rollout of v2-serving). Any link? @sarah?

sarah: that deployment finished at 2866549500, healthchecks passed. no rollback triggered.

lee: dumping recent gateway logs: ```
[2026-03-14T02:00:12Z] GET /v1/generate 502 upstream_reset model-backend-27
[2026-03-14T02:00:12Z] GET /v1/generate 502 upstream_timeout model-backend-13
[2026-03-14T02:00:13Z] POST /v1/chat 504 connection_closed by model-backend-19
```

anya: running `kubectl get pods -n prod inference-pool -o wide` to check restarts and node pressure

infra-bot: Node pool gpu-west1-3 CPU 64% MEM 79% GPU 95% - pod restarts: model-backend-13=3, model-backend-19=4, model-backend-27=0

lee: seems like a few backends are flapping under GPU mem pressure. could be OOM or bad batch size change.

anya: can we throttle request batching or force small batch config? I can push quick config patch to route to smaller batch sizes for this pool.

lee: do it. create canary route -> route requests away from model-backend-13 and model-backend-19. fallback to cpu-backend as temporary if needed.

anya: patch applied: `cfg.inference.pool.batch_size=8` for pool gpu-west1-3, routing weight change to divert 60% to spare pool.

ops-oncall: Seeing immediate drop in 5xx graph on alert dashboard, from 12.4% -> 6.2% in ~90s. Nice.

mike: any customer-facing errors? support triage?

lee: quick check: customer error rate aligns with internal 5xx. Top impacted tenants: sandbox-proj, querybot-svc. Opening support flag and sending initial message to CS.

sarah: started a temporary horizontal scale: increased replica count for model-backend by +2 in spare pool.

infra-bot: HorizontalPodAutoscaler scaled model-backend-spare from 3 -> 5.

lee: logs post-change show reduced upstream timeouts. still seeing a few 502s from model-backend-13 which I'm cordoning.

anya: cordon+drain model-backend-13, and add it to maintenance. `kubectl cordon model-backend-13 && kubectl drain model-backend-13 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data`

infra-bot: model-backend-13 drained. restart scheduled.

lee: confirmed error rate down to 2.1% over last 2m. paging threshold cleared?

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Alert resolved - metric=http_5xx_rate back under threshold for 5m - INC-8432 auto-closed (notes: diverted traffic, scaled spare pool, cordoned flapping node).

anya: filing follow-up: looks like a memory regression in recent model runtime that increases batch memory usage; we'll need a postmortem. creating ticket INF-1129.

mike: customer outreach: CS notified top impacted customers, offering small credits and explanation.

lee: leaving detailed runbook notes in INC-8432 and passing to next oncall @sarah for 06:00-14:00 handoff.

sarah: taking handoff. steps: monitor 5xx for 30m, confirm drained node back to pool only after sanity tests, coordinate with model-runtime team for regression analysis.

ops-oncall: adding reactions :thumbsup: and marking incident as handled.

anya: quick snippet for postmortem template: impact = ~4% of requests for 18min, mitigation = routing + scale + cordon, root cause candidate = model runtime memory regression after v2-serving rollout, next steps = revert or patch batch mem usage, add autoscale threshold, add pre-merge regression test for batch mem.

lee: thanks everyone. closing thread after handoff notes posted.

incident-bot: Postmortem ticket INF-1129 created and linked to INC-8432. Reminder: runbook owners @infra-team to validate new autoscale thresholds.
